reading.body:
Grain is a meeting recording platform that captures video, audio, and transcripts from calls and in-person meetings, then uses AI to generate summaries, highlights, and coaching suggestions for sales and customer success teams.

The company's model depends on processing large volumes of meeting data through external AI systems like Claude and ChatGPT. This positions Grain as a data aggregator and conditioning layer for AI inference rather than a compute provider itself. Teams using Grain feed customer calls, sales conversations, and internal discussions into the platform, which then routes the resulting transcripts and video through third-party models. The business scales with adoption across teams, which means more meetings recorded and more inference requests sent downstream.

Grain's stated policy of not using customer data for model training distinguishes it from some competitors but does not eliminate the compute footprint. Every meeting processed still requires inference cycles, storage, and transmission bandwidth. At scale across growing teams, this represents material demand on the grid and data center capacity of the AI providers Grain integrates with.

The data provided covers the company's product category, founding date, location, and regulatory exposure in California, but does not include user numbers, inference volume, or specifics on which AI providers receive the most requests from Grain's platform. These omissions mean the actual compute demand Grain drives remains opaque.

profile_text.body:
Grain is an AI notetaker and conversation intelligence platform, according to its own site. The company was founded in 2018 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Grain records video calls, Slack huddles, and in-person meetings, and the company says it captures all meeting content, including video, desktop captured audio, and the resulting transcripts and notes. It describes its audience as any team that relies on meetings, with a stated specialty in small to mid-market and enterprise sales, customer success, and product teams. The site also says meeting data can be delivered to Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI tools.

On pricing, Grain offers a free plan with unlimited meetings for teams, and paid plans start at $15/month per user. The free plan includes unlimited recordings, transcripts, basic AI notes, a collaborative workspace, and desktop capture, with a 45-minute meeting limit and 90-day meeting history. Paid plans add advanced AI, conversational intelligence, priority support, unlimited meeting length, and unlimited meeting history. The company says it supports over 130 languages for transcription and AI notes, with over 100 additional languages beyond the most common ones, and states that neither Grain nor its subprocessors use customer data for model training.

The product tracked here is Grain, listed under Notes, Knowledge and Meetings, with meeting recording AI, highlight clips, CRM integration, and consent and sharing features. A California law exposure count of 237 is recorded, with no individual cases listed. No MCP server is listed for the company.
